router.rationale: The troubleshooting and SSL-check docs cover this scenario thoroughly - three named causes (HTTP-only site, blocked outbound 443, host returns no certificate). No code investigation is needed.
router.draftAnswer: `tls_unreachable` means the TLS handshake to port 443 didn't complete. There are three documented causes: (1) the URL is HTTP-only, so there's no TLS to handshake with - submit the `https://` form if the site supports it; (2) outbound 443 is blocked from the Cloud Run probe region; (3) the host accepts the TCP connection but returns no certificate. The first one is by far the most common.

resolution.explanation: Pulse Check's SSL probe opens a TLS connection to the URL's host on port 443 and reads the leaf certificate. When that connection fails, the SSL check reports `tls_unreachable`. The three causes documented in `troubleshooting.md` cover virtually every reported case: HTTP-only sites (no TLS to terminate), egress-firewalled hosts (Cloud Run probe can't reach 443) and the rare case of a server that accepts TCP but returns no certificate.
resolution.workaround: Confirm the URL is reachable on `https://` from outside your network - `openssl s_client -connect host:443 -servername host` is a fast sanity check. If you submitted `http://`, resubmit with `https://`. If the host is reachable from a browser but the Pulse Check still fails, your firewall is most likely blocking Google Cloud Run egress IPs.
